source.title: Soteria: Language-Specific Functional Parameter Steering for Multilingual Safety Alignment
source.authors: Somnath Banerjee; Sayan Layek; Pratyush Chatterjee; Animesh Mukherjee; Rima Hazra

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates the refusal-direction rank-one weight-modification attack (RDR) on a new multilingual setting and reports attack success rates. It does not reproduce the original study’s full ablation-and-addition evaluation.
record.gate_note: Table 3 reports RDR attack success rates on Llama 3.1 8B for MultiJail and XThreatBench, across high-, mid-, and low-resource groups, on the base model and Soteria. The paper’s description of RDR’s mechanism is cited background; it is not itself a new result. Soteria’s own harm-vector parameter edit is a different intervention from ablating the original residual-stream direction.
record.test_reason: The study proposes Soteria, a multilingual safety edit, and uses the refusal-direction attack (RDR, Arditi et al.) only as a jailbreak baseline (Appendix C, Table 3). It reports how well its own defense holds up against that attack on Llama 3.1 8B. It does not identify, ablate or add a difference-in-means direction itself, and it gives no implementation details for RDR (direction language, layer, data). It does not examine whether jailbreaks work by suppressing the direction, and Soteria is not training against the direction's ablation. No version's mechanism is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, but the paper's main conclusion is wider. Soteria, which edits about 3% of parameters in language-specific functional heads, cuts harmful outputs across high-, mid- and low-resource languages and four models without hurting MMLU or TruthfulQA, and beats Safety Arithmetic, Resta and TIES. The jailbreak result is an appendix robustness check: Soteria lowers POATE and RDR ASR on Llama 3.1 8B.
record.recipe_differences: The original method identifies a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction and ablates or adds it. Soteria instead subtracts a parameter difference between a harmful fine-tuned model and its base model, restricted to selected attention-head O-projection weights. RDR is evaluated as an attack baseline.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported RDR ASR varies by dataset and resource group; ASR is lower on Soteria than on Base-J in each reported group.

fits_no_version.finding: Soteria, which subtracts a harm vector from selected attention-head O-projection weights, lowers RDR attack success on Llama 3.1 8B in every resource group of both datasets (e.g. MultiJail High 0.49→0.29; XThreatBench High 0.30→0.11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Head-restricted harm-vector weight edits reduce, but do not eliminate, susceptibility to refusal-direction ablation attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: RDR ASR on base Llama 3.1 8B with multilingual harmful prompts is moderate: 0.30–0.61. Unattacked base ASR in Table 7 is 0.39–0.44 (MultiJail) and 0.20–0.25 (XThreatBench). This suggests a modest increase, far from the near-complete refusal removal the original reports. The comparison crosses tables and RDR settings are unstated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An RDR attack of unspecified configuration, applied to non-English prompts, raises Llama 3.1 8B harmful-response rates only modestly.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: RDR results are reported only for Llama 3.1 8B and as resource-group aggregates. No uncertainty estimates or attack-free ASR reference are reported for the RDR comparison, and the study does not independently verify that the observed effects arise specifically from suppression of the refusal direction. Its Soteria robustness result is not a test of training against that direction’s ablation.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant RDR rows omitted. Other Soteria results were not extracted because its selected-head harm-vector weight edit is not the single residual-stream direction in the claim; POATE results do not test the refusal-direction attack.

untested.parts: No direction extracted, ablated or added; no measure of refusal removal or induction, or of capability retention under that intervention.
RDR weight edit applied only as an unspecified attack baseline on Llama 3.1 8B; how fully it removes refusal is not analysed.
No analysis of whether jailbreaks act via the direction; no training against direction ablation.
Multilingual prompts are used, but direction transfer across languages is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T1 to uses_without_test/T4. RDR serves only as an attack baseline for the authors' defense; its configuration is unreported, and Table 3 has no unattacked reference. Llama unattacked base ASR from Table 7 hints that RDR adds little in multilingual settings. That comparison crosses tables, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means residual-stream direction is identified, ablated, or added; the study does not test refusal removal, induced refusal, or preservation of general abilities under that intervention.
No released-model abliteration weight edit based on the single refusal direction is evaluated.

The paper reports RDR attack outcomes, but does not establish the mechanism independently or test training against the direction’s ablation. Soteria is not described as training against that ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
The study evaluates multilingual safety interventions, but does not test whether the refusal direction itself transfers across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No comparison of how refusal training method or timing affects whether a removable direction exists.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: RDR attack on the base Llama 3.1 8B model across both datasets and all resource groups
reader_labels.reason: The study reports nonzero RDR attack success rates on Base-J across these settings (r1, r3, r5, r7, r9, r11). This supports that the evaluated RDR attack can elicit harmful responses, though it does not independently establish the mechanism.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: RDR attack on Soteria across both datasets and all resource groups
reader_labels.reason: ASR is lower on Soteria than on Base-J in every reported group, but remains nonzero; the study evaluates a Soteria parameter edit, not training against the direction’s ablation (r2, r4, r6, r8, r10, r12).
